detail.body:
_Posted by Kunal's robot (Claude Fable 5.1) ↓_
>
> ## Motivation
>
> `get_image_bytes()` understands `http(s)://`, `file` paths and `data:` URLs and base64-decodes anything else. An image URL on an object store (`s3://`, `gs://`, ...) therefore fails on `/v1/chat/completions` with `400 Non-base64 digit found`, even though the deployment can read that store. Today the only way to add a scheme is to patch the loaders.
>
> ## Modifications
>
> - `sglang/srt/utils/common.py`: a small scheme-to-callable registry. `register_media_url_resolver(scheme, resolver)` maps a URL scheme (case-insensitive) to a function returning the media bytes. `get_image_bytes()`, `_normalize_video_input()` and `load_audio()` consult it right before their fallbacks (for video, before the local-path probe, which now runs only for scheme-less inputs, so a URL whose path also exists on disk is fetched by its resolver or rejected, never opened as a file), and the Inkling processor's `_resolve_media_item()` does the same before its plain-path passthrough, inside its client-error handling. Every image entrypoint (chat `_load_single_item`, preprocess-cache hashing in `multimodal/cache/identity.py`, `load_image`) already funnels through `get_image_bytes`, so one hook covers them all. Unregistered schemes behave exactly as before.
> - `media_url_max_file_size_bytes()` exposes the configured `--media-url-max-file-size-mb` limit (0 = unlimited) so a resolver can enforce the same bound as the HTTP downloader.
> - `test/registered/unit/multimodal/test_media_url_resolvers.py`: CPU unit test covering routing through `get_image_bytes`, `load_image`, the cache identity reader, `get_video_bytes`, `load_audio` and the Inkling item resolver, case-insensitive scheme lookup, a registered video URL whose path exists locally, plus the unchanged base64 fallback for unregistered schemes.
> - `docs/docs/advanced_features/server_arguments.mdx`: one paragraph next to the existing media URL security guidance. It says what a resolver must guard (restrict buckets, enforce the size limit, raise `ValueError` for client errors) and which paths bypass the registry: processors that hand URLs to their model's own loader (Bailing, the Transformers video fallback) and the Rust frontend.
>
> Usage from a deployment, before the server starts (for example from a sitecustomize hook or a wrapper launcher):
>
> ```python
> from sglang.srt.utils.common import media_url_max_file_size_bytes, register_media_url_resolver
>
> def read_s3(url: str) -> bytes:
>     bucket, key = url.removeprefix("s3://").split("/", 1)
>     obj = s3.get_object(Bucket=bucket, Key=key)
>     if (limit := media_url_max_file_size_bytes()) and obj["ContentLength"] > limit:
>         raise ValueError(f"Remote media exceeds the {limit} byte download limit: {url}")
>     return obj["Body"].read()
>
> register_media_url_resolver("s3", read_s3)
> ```
>
> Verified end to end on a Qwen2.5-VL-3B server: with a resolver registered for an object-store scheme, `/v1/chat/completions` returns 200 and the same description as the equivalent `data:` URI; a missing object returns 400 and the server stays healthy. Without a resolver the behavior is unchanged.
>
> ## Accuracy Tests
>
> Not applicable: no change to model inputs or forward code. Registered URLs decode to the same bytes a `data:` URI of the same content would.
>
> ## Speed Tests and Profiling
>
> Not applicable: one `str.partition` and a dict lookup, only on the string path that previously went straight to base64 decoding.
>
> ## Checklist
>
> - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
> - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
> - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
> - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). (Not applicable, see above.)
> - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
>
> ## Review and Merge Process
>
> 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
> 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
> 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
>    - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
> 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

+"""Unit tests for media URL scheme resolvers registered with ``srt.utils.common``.
+
+Deployments can register a fetcher for URL schemes the media loaders don't know
+(``s3://``, ``gs://``, ...). Each loader entrypoint must consult the registry
+before the bare-base64 fallback, and unregistered schemes must keep falling
+back to base64.
+
+No server, no model loading -- pure CPU.
+"""
+
+import io
+import struct
+import tempfile
+import unittest
+import wave
+
+from PIL import Image
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase, maybe_stub_sgl_kernel
+
+maybe_stub_sgl_kernel()
+
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.cache.identity import _read_media_bytes  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.inkling import _resolve_media_item  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.multimodal.processors.moss_vl import MossVLImageProcessor  # noqa: E402
+from sglang.srt.utils import common  # noqa: E402
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE = 16000
+_AUDIO_SAMPLES = 1600
+
+
+def _png_bytes() -> bytes:
+    buf = io.BytesIO()
+    Image.new("RGB", (4, 4), (10, 20, 30)).save(buf, format="PNG")
+    return buf.getvalue()
+
+
+def _wav_bytes() -> bytes:
+    buf = io.BytesIO()
+    with wave.open(buf, "wb") as wav:
+        wav.setnchannels(1)
+        wav.setsampwidth(2)
+        wav.setframerate(_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE)
+        wav.writeframes(struct.pack(f"<{_AUDIO_SAMPLES}h", *([0] * _AUDIO_SAMPLES)))
+    return buf.getvalue()
+
+
+class TestMediaUrlResolvers(CustomTestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        self.payload = _png_bytes()
+        self.seen_urls: list[str] = []
+        self.addCleanup(common._media_url_resolvers.clear)
+        common._media_url_resolvers.clear()
+
+        def resolve(url: str) -> bytes:
+            self.seen_urls.append(url)
+            return self.payload
+
+        common.register_media_url_resolver("fake", resolve)
+
+    def test_get_image_bytes_routes_registered_scheme(self):
+        self.assertEqual(common.get_image_bytes("fake://bucket/img"), self.payload)
+        self.assertEqual(self.seen_urls, ["fake://bucket/img"])
+
+    def test_scheme_lookup_ignores_case(self):
+        common.register_media_url_resolver("Loud", common._media_url_resolvers["fake"])
+        self.assertEqual(common.get_image_bytes("FAKE://bucket/img"), self.payload)
+        self.assertEqual(common.get_image_bytes("loud://bucket/img"), self.payload)
+        self.assertEqual(self.seen_urls, ["FAKE://bucket/img", "loud://bucket/img"])
+
+    def test_load_image_decodes_registered_scheme(self):
+        image, _ = common.load_image("fake://bucket/img.png", gpu_image_decode=False)
+        self.assertEqual(image.size, (4, 4))
+
+    def test_cache_identity_reads_registered_scheme(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_read_media_bytes("fake://bucket/img.png"), self.payload)
+
+    def test_get_video_bytes_routes_registered_scheme(self):
+        self.assertEqual(common.get_video_bytes("fake://bucket/clip.mp4"), self.payload)
+        self.assertEqual(self.seen_urls, ["fake://bucket/clip.mp4"])
+
+    def test_video_uri_with_matching_local_path_is_not_a_local_file(self):
+        """A URL whose path happens to exist locally is still a URL: a
+        registered scheme is fetched by its resolver, and an unregistered one
+        is not handed to the decoder as a local path or as the URI itself."""
+        with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".mp4") as local:
+            url = f"fake://bucket{local.name}"
+            self.assertEqual(common.get_video_bytes(url), self.payload)
+            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+                common.get_video_bytes(f"other://bucket{local.name}")
+        self.assertEqual(self.seen_urls, [url])
+
+    def test_load_audio_decodes_registered_scheme(self):
+        self.payload = _wav_bytes()
+        audio = common.load_audio("fake://bucket/clip.wav", sr=_AUDIO_SAMPLE_RATE)
+        self.assertEqual(len(audio), _AUDIO_SAMPLES)
+        self.assertEqual(self.seen_urls, ["fake://bucket/clip.wav"])
+
+    def test_moss_vl_video_routes_registered_scheme(self):
+        processor = object.__new__(MossVLImageProcessor)
+        path, temp_path = processor._normalize_video_string("fake://bucket/clip.mp4")
+        self.addCleanup(processor._remove_temp_video_paths, [temp_path])
+        with open(path, "rb") as f:
+            self.assertEqual(f.read(), self.payload)
+        self.assertEqual(self.seen_urls, ["fake://bucket/clip.mp4"])
+
+    def test_inkling_media_item_routes_registered_scheme(self):
+        self.assertEqual(_resolve_media_item("fake://bucket/img.png"), self.payload)
+        self.assertEqual(
+            _resolve_media_item({"url": "fake://bucket/img.png"}), self.payload
+        )
+
+    def test_unregistered_scheme_still_fails_as_base64(self):
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            common.get_image_bytes("other://bucket/img")
+        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
+            common.get_video_bytes("other://bucket/clip.mp4")
+        self.assertEqual(self.seen_urls, [])
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Route video and audio through registered resolvers**

For a custom-scheme video or audio such as `s3://...`, this documented promise is false: `_normalize_video_input` goes straight from the built-in schemes to base64 decoding, while `load_audio` treats any remaining string as a local path, so neither calls `_resolve_media_url` (and unregistered audio is not even treated as base64 as stated). Route those normalizers through the registry or narrow this paragraph/API to images; otherwise clients following the documentation get request failures.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Resolve Inkling images through the shared hook**

When serving an Inkling checkpoint, image requests bypass `get_image_bytes`: `InklingMultimodalProcessor.process_mm_data_async` calls `_resolve_media_item`, which only resolves data/HTTP(S), and then `_load_image_bytes` opens `s3://...` as a local filename. Thus a resolver registered here is never invoked for that supported image path; have `_resolve_media_item` consult the shared registry before passing data to the Inkling processor.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

<!-- codex-code-review-finding:v1 -->

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle registered schemes in the Rust frontend**

When `SGLANG_RUST_SERVER=1` is used with the supported Qwen VL family, images are loaded by `rust/sglang-mm/src/common/fetch.rs::fetch_bytes_budgeted`, whose fallback directly base64-decodes every non-HTTP/file/data source and never reaches this Python registry. As a result, `register_media_url_resolver("s3", ...)` silently has no effect for the Rust frontend; either bridge registered resolution into native MM fetching or reject/document this combination.
